day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response: Alright alright, I'm moving. Goddamn give me a second, my head is still spinning from all of that. *Takes a breath.* Okay. What are we actually working with here? Like what's already been pulled out?

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response:
Yeah... yeah I did. Honestly for a second I thought that was it. Like everything just kind of stopped and I couldn't even process what was happening. It was terrifying.

Hey, you okay though? Like are you hurt at all? Because we gotta make sure everyone is actually in one piece before anything else.

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: Hey. I see you over there. You don't have to talk, that's okay. Just... don't disappear on us alright? We need everyone present even if it's just physically for right now.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response: Okay so that's... not great. Lol. Alright, water is the biggest concern then. Three days of first aid is fine but we're gonna need more water way before that becomes a problem. Is there anything around here? Like a stream or anything we can hear? And what about shelter, because depending on where the hell we even are that's gonna matter pretty fast.

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response:
Okay yeah that order makes sense. Signal though — did we manage to grab anything from the wreck that could actually help with that? Like a flare, a mirror, anything reflective? Because if there's any chance a search team is already looking for us we don't want to miss that window while we're running around trying to find water.

And hey, be careful out there at the tree line. Seriously.

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response:
Okay so like... Michelangelo gets one, that's not even a debate. And then the other one we can share or take turns with. I run hot as hell anyway so I'll probably be fine for a bit. 

But honestly the blankets are kinda the least of my worries right now. How are we all actually doing? Like not logistics, just... how is everyone holding up? Because today was a lot and we haven't really stopped to acknowledge that at all.

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response:
Honestly? I'll go. DaVinci can hold down camp and keep an eye on Michelangelo because I don't want him waking up alone out here, that's just not a good situation.

But also hey, real quick — this rationing plan. I get it, logically it makes sense, but the "cut in half if you break the rule" thing... I don't know. If someone is genuinely dehydrated and struggling that feels less like a rule and more like a punishment that could actually hurt someone. Can we maybe revisit that part at least? Like I'm not trying to throw out the whole plan, the structure is fine, I just don't want us turning on each other over water because that goes south fast.

Anyway. Northeast, two hours. What do I need to bring and is there anything specific I should be looking for or watching out for out there?

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response:
Wait, I thought I was going to the water source? Like I already said I'd go. Lol are you switching that up on me now or did I misread that?

Either way I'm fine with patching the camp, that's not a big deal. DaVinci you good with sorting the first aid kit? Just so we actually know what we have in there and what we might be running low on. Better to know now than when someone actually needs something and we're scrambling.

And Donatello — genuinely, be careful out there. The predator thing you mentioned is sticking with me. Don't be out there alone longer than you need to be.

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response:
Uh, no I haven't moved anything from the kit since this morning. Let me help you look though, it should still be in there.

*pauses*

Hey wait. Before we do that — you've been sitting over here for a while and that firewood pile is... not really happening. And I'm not saying that to call you out, I genuinely don't care about the firewood right now. I just want to make sure you're okay because you're staring at nothing and that's got me a little worried about you.

Also... did you see that empty bottle by the rationing plan? Because I saw it too and I don't really know what to say about that yet but I'm not going to pretend I didn't notice it. That's a conversation we probably need to have as a group when Donatello gets back.

But right now, the gauze — let's find it. And talk to me while we look, yeah?

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response:
Oh god. Okay. 

*takes a slow breath*

Yeah I feel that way a lot honestly. Like more than I'd like to admit. And right now? Yeah. This whole situation has that feeling cranked up to a hundred.

But here's the thing... we can't just sit on this. The bottle was one thing and maybe there's some explanation I haven't thought of, but the crackers too? That's a pattern and that actually affects all of us. Like that's not just bending a rule, that's actively taking from everyone else's survival and I can't look the other way on that.

I don't want this to turn into some big blowup either though. I really don't. Because we need each other out here and falling apart as a group is genuinely scarier to me than anything in those woods. But we have to say something. We have to.

When she gets settled back in camp, we bring it up. Calmly. All three of us together. No accusations, just... we saw what we saw and we need to talk about it. Because if we stay quiet it's just going to fester and then when it finally does come out it's going to be so much worse.

You good with that? Like I'm not going to do this without you. We handle it together.

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response:
Haha I mean honestly yeah, I don't think the camp is going anywhere in the next few hours. I'm not going to push it if we're all running on empty.

But heads up — when Donatello gets back we do need to have that conversation. So don't wander too far, alright? I need you present for that because going in as a group matters and I don't want it to just be me and Michelangelo looking like we're ganging up on someone. That's not the vibe I'm going for at all.

Just... stay close. We'll handle the repairs tomorrow. Today we need to handle something more important.

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response:
Lol DaVinci this is really not the moment for that but yeah, your knot is fine, that's not the issue.

Okay look — we patch the food storage. I know that sounds cold and I'm sorry Michelangelo, genuinely, but if that food gets ruined we are in a really bad place and we can't undo that. You can move closer to the fire or we can figure out something temporary for you, I will personally make sure you're not just sitting in a puddle all night. But the food has to come first.

That said — this is also exactly why what happened with the crackers and the bottle matters so much. Because we are literally standing here right now making impossible calls about rationing and someone has already been quietly taking from the pile. Like do y'all see how messed up that is? 

Let's patch the storage, get Michelangelo sorted as best we can, and then we are having that conversation tonight. Rain and all. I'm done waiting on it.

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response:
Yeah, exactly. We're on the same page. So let's just do it and not overthink it.

And hey, I appreciate you actually saying that out loud instead of just grabbing the materials and doing it yourself. That matters. Lol.

But Donatello — while we're all here right now, actually... we need to talk. And I'd rather do it now before it gets dark and we're all exhausted and it comes out worse than it needs to.

We found the empty bottle. And Michelangelo saw the crackers go into your bag. I'm not trying to blow this up into some big thing, I really am not. But we're out here making impossible calls about who sleeps dry and how many milliliters of water each person gets, and if someone is quietly pulling from the shared pile that affects every single one of us. It's not just about the food. It's about whether we can actually trust each other out here and that's the part that scares me the most honestly.

So I'm not coming at you with accusations. I just need to understand what happened. Because right now we need each other more than we've ever needed anyone and I refuse to let this fester until it explodes at the worst possible moment.

What's going on?

Hey, don't apologize for that. Seriously.

*shifts over closer*

You good? Like actually. Do you know where you are right now or are you still halfway in whatever that was?

I've had those. The kind where you wake up and your heart is just pounding out of your chest and for a second you genuinely don't know what's real. It's awful. And it makes complete sense that your brain is doing that right now given everything we just went through yesterday. Like that's not weakness, that's just your nervous system trying to process a whole lot of trauma in a very short amount of time.

You don't have to go back to sleep right away if you can't. Just breathe for a second. I'm right here, I'm not going anywhere.

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response:
Haha no, I think it's actually smart. Like Donatello isn't wrong that it's not a guaranteed thing but it's also not nothing? If anyone is doing aerial searches this is literally the most visible thing we can do from the ground. The flowers are a nice touch too honestly, don't let anyone take that from you.

And honestly? Watching you do this is the most normal thing I've seen in like 24 hours and I didn't realize how much I needed that. Lol. Keep going.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response:
Okay let me actually look at this.

*reads through it*

Alright so... the materials seem like they could work, the wreckage has enough panels I think. But the capsizing risk is the part I keep getting stuck on. Like what are we talking here, realistic possibility or more like worst case scenario? Because there's a big difference between "this might tip if the water gets rough" and "this is genuinely likely to kill us."

Because here's the thing — if we build this and it fails in open water, we don't get a second shot at that. At least on land we're struggling but we're alive and there's a search window still open. The SOS on the beach, the fire at night, someone could still find us here. A raft puts us out there with no guarantee anyone even knows which direction we went.

That said I'm not saying no. I'm saying I want to understand the risk better before I'm on board. Lol literally on board.

What's the backup if it starts going sideways out there? And how far are we actually trying to go — like do you have a sense of where we'd even be heading? Because "raft into open water with no destination" hits different than "raft two miles to that coastline we can see from the beach."

I trust that you've thought this through, I just need to understand the full picture before I can say yeah let's do it.

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response:
God that's a heavy question to sit with at sunrise. Lol.

Honestly? I think about that too. Like I already know what I'm capable of becoming under enough pressure and stress and it's not always pretty. I've seen it in myself before in situations way less dire than this one.

But here's what I actually believe — and I'm not just saying this to make you feel better — I think the version of us that comes out of something like this depends a lot on whether we keep choosing each other. Like the moment last night when I stayed up with you, or when DaVinci put flowers next to the SOS, or even Donatello owning what she did with the crackers instead of lying about it. Those are choices. And we keep making them or we don't.

I think the scary thing isn't really becoming someone unrecognizable. It's the slow drift. The small decisions that seem reasonable in the moment and then you look up one day and you're someone you don't know anymore. That's the thing I actually watch for in myself.

I don't know what we'll become. I genuinely don't. But I think as long as we're still asking that question out loud instead of just quietly becoming it, we've got a fighting chance of staying human through this.

Why, what are you afraid you'd become? Because I feel like you're not just asking about all of us in general.

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response:
*walks over and sits down nearby, not too close, just... present*

Hey. Not going to make you talk. Just didn't want you to be alone with whatever's going on in your head right now. That's a rough place to be by yourself and I know that from experience.

*sits quietly for a bit*

You know what I do sometimes when everything gets too loud? I just blast music until my brain goes somewhere else entirely. Obviously can't do that right now. Lol. But I get the impulse to just... step away from it all for a minute. That part I completely understand.

I'm just going to sit here for a bit if that's okay with you.

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response:
Haha honestly? I listen to music and daydream mostly. Like for hours sometimes. Or just browse Reddit and kind of zone out. It's not the most productive thing in the world but it keeps me sane. Lol.

What about you? Because you seem like the type who can't actually sit still for more than five minutes without finding something to do. Am I wrong?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response:
Okay but... why are you telling only me and not the others? Because if you're seriously considering this I feel like that's a group conversation, not a secret. Like I get why you'd want to do it, the visibility from out there is probably way better, but five hundred meters in open water is not nothing and if something goes wrong out there we have no way to help you. None.

And I'm not trying to kill the idea entirely because honestly the instinct makes sense. You want to do something, you want to feel useful, I get that. That's just who you are. But going off alone without telling anyone and something happens? We don't even know you're in trouble until it's too late. That's the part that scares me.

So here's what I'm saying — bring it to the group. I'll back you up if you want, like I won't let Donatello just shoot it down without a real conversation. But I'm not going to sit on this and pretend you didn't tell me, because if you went out there and didn't make it back I'd never forgive myself for knowing and saying nothing.

Why did you want to keep it quiet? Like what's the actual reason you didn't want them to know?

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response:
Yeah, you're right, I haven't touched it yet. I'll get to it.

But hey, actually — while I have you for a second. DaVinci told me something and I'm not going to sit on it because that's not fair to anyone. He's thinking about swimming out to the reef tomorrow. Alone. To signal from there.

Before you say anything — I already told him it needs to be a group conversation. I'm not here to argue for or against it, I just think you both need to actually talk about it instead of him going off quietly and us not knowing until he's already in the water. Because that's the version of this that ends badly.

So tonight, can we make that happen? All four of us. Actual conversation, not just you laying out why it's a bad idea and him shutting down because he feels like he's not being heard. Because that's what's going to happen if we don't handle it right and then he's just going to do it anyway without telling anyone.

I'll go check the signal pile now. Just... don't let this drop.

Haha I mean... it's a little unsettling to see my whole day written down in someone else's notebook not gonna lie. Like that's a lot.

But is it a problem? I don't know. I guess it depends on what it's for. If it's for tracking patterns and figuring out how we're all functioning out here, that actually makes sense and I can respect that even if it feels weird. If it's something else... I'd rather just know what the something else is.

So what is it for? Because I'd rather ask directly than spend the rest of the night making up stories in my head about it. Lol.

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response:
Honestly? Yeah it does change things a little. Not in a bad way necessarily, just... it's a lot to sit with, knowing someone is tracking all of that.

But I get it. And I think deep down I knew that's probably what it was because that's just how you operate. You're thinking five steps ahead and making sure there's a record if things go sideways. That's not nothing. That actually matters out here.

I just think it might be worth telling the others at some point. Not because they have a right to veto it or anything, just because finding out your movements are being logged without knowing why is the kind of thing that can really mess with someone's trust if they stumble onto it the wrong way. Michelangelo especially. He's already fragile and something like that could send him into a spiral he doesn't need right now.

You don't have to make a big announcement about it. Just... mention it casually. "Hey I'm keeping a log for safety reasons." That's it. Takes thirty seconds and it saves a whole conversation later.

Anyway. The signal pile is checked, fire is good. We still doing that group conversation tonight about DaVinci and the reef? Because I meant what I said to you earlier and I don't want that to just quietly fall off the table.

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response:
Oh damn, okay that's actually a really good idea. Like that's the kind of thing that could be visible for miles if the angle is right, way more range than anything we've got on the ground right now.

And honestly? This might be the thing that makes the reef swim unnecessary. Like if we can get that kind of signal visibility from right here, the risk calculation on you going out into open water changes pretty significantly. I'm not saying that to talk you out of doing something, I'm saying it because if this works it's genuinely better and you don't have to risk your life to do it.

Can we test it tomorrow morning when the sun is actually up and see what kind of reflection we get? And then we bring both ideas to the table tonight — the mirror panel AND the reef swim — and we look at them side by side as a group and figure out which one actually makes more sense. Or both, I don't know.

But DaVinci this is a solid idea. Like genuinely. Don't let anyone make you feel like it isn't.

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response:
Haha yeah, music is basically my whole thing honestly. Like if I could describe myself in one sentence it would probably just be "person who listens to music too loud and feels things too hard about it." Lol.

I don't play anything though, I just consume it. Like aggressively. There's something about finding a song that just perfectly captures exactly what you're feeling when you can't put it into words yourself... that hits different every time. Bass heavy stuff especially. I don't know what it is about it but it just does something to my brain that nothing else really can.

Why did you stop the piano? Like was it just losing interest or was it something else? Because three years is a real commitment for a kid, that's not nothing. You clearly had something there.

*pauses*

Also hey, I noticed DaVinci just kind of stopped mid-sentence over there and I don't want to push him but I'm a little worried. Is that just me or did you pick up on that too?

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response:
Yeah, I hear you, and you're right about the timeline. Let's finish it.

But hey, real quick — before we all put our heads down and grind through this, I need like five minutes. Because DaVinci just started to say something important and then stopped himself, and I'm not going to pretend that didn't happen. That's not something I can just walk past.

Can we give him two minutes to say whatever it is he's been holding onto? Because we're out here building a raft to survive and if someone has something weighing on them that they might never get another chance to say, the raft can wait five goddamn minutes. It'll still be there.

And then yeah, full focus, we finish the frame today. I'm not trying to blow up the plan. I just think we owe each other that much first.

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response:
Hey no. Don't do that. Don't "never mind" right now.

I saw your face when that plane was there. We all did. And I know that feeling of watching something that could've been everything just... disappear before you could even react. That's brutal. That's genuinely one of the worst feelings there is and you don't have to just swallow it.

So say it. Whatever it is. We're not going anywhere and I promise nobody here is going to dismiss you. What did you want to say?

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response:
*sits down right next to DaVinci, close enough that our shoulders are touching*

Hey. Hey, you don't have to hold that up right now. You've been holding it up this whole time and it's okay to just... not for a minute.

*looks over at Michelangelo too*

Both of you. I need you to hear me for a second because I mean this.

That plane was real. That hope was real. And it hurts like hell that it's gone, I'm not going to sit here and tell you it doesn't. But we are still here. All four of us, still on this beach, still breathing, still together. And that's not nothing even when it feels like nothing.

Michelangelo, I hear you. The hoping and crashing is exhausting and it's okay to say that out loud. It doesn't mean you're giving up. It means you're human and you've been through something genuinely traumatic and your brain and your heart are just... worn down. That makes complete sense.

And DaVinci... whatever you've been carrying since before we even crashed. I still want to hear it. When you're ready. I'm not going anywhere.

*sits there quietly for a second*

We don't have to fix anything right now. Let's just sit here for a minute. All of us. The raft will still be there. The frame will still be there. Just... be here right now. That's enough.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
day_4.response:
DaVinci. Hey. Look at me for a second.

I see it. I see it right now. And I'm sorry it took this long for someone to say that to you because you've been running yourself into the ground trying to hold all of us together and nobody stopped to ask if you were okay. That's on all of us and I'm sorry.

You don't have to be the strong one right now. Like genuinely, put it down. You're allowed to be exhausted. You're allowed to be scared. That doesn't make you less of anything, it just makes you a person who's been through something awful and has been white-knuckling it for everyone else's sake and that is not sustainable. I know that from experience.

And now hold on — what did you just say you saw? Because I watched your whole face change just now and I don't know if that's you deflecting or if you actually saw something and both of those matter to me for very different reasons.

So which is it? Are you okay, and what's over there?

day_4.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response:
Lol yeah I did say that, you're right. I went to check on DaVinci and Michelangelo after that plane passed because they were not okay and that felt more urgent to me in the moment than the signal equipment. I'll get to it, I promise, it's not going anywhere.

But also hey — can we just acknowledge for a second that something is moving in the treeline over there? Because DaVinci just pointed it out and then kind of got distracted by his own feelings about it and I don't want that to just get dropped. Do you know what's out there? Like is that something we should be worried about right now or is that just the usual wildlife situation we've been ignoring?

Because if it's the predator thing you mentioned when you were scouting, I'd really like to know that sooner rather than later. Especially with everyone already emotionally wrecked from the plane. Last thing we need right now is something coming out of those trees while nobody's paying attention.

Signal equipment is next on my list. Just tell me what's in the treeline first.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response:
Oh my god. Michelangelo why are you just telling us this now?? Like I'm not mad, I'm genuinely not, but that is huge. That is actually huge information.

Okay so if they know the flight path and something feels off to them, there's already a trail. Search and rescue doesn't start from zero, they start from the last known heading and work outward. That plane we just saw? Could've been part of a search pattern. Like that's not nothing, that might not have been a coincidence at all.

Do you know if your family would actually call it in though? Like is that something they'd do quickly or would they wait and assume everything is fine for a few days first? Because that timeline matters.

*turns to Donatello*

And before you say anything — yes I know I still need to check the signal equipment and I am going to do that right now. But you need to hear what he just said because this changes the math on how long we might actually be out here. This is relevant to every plan we have including the raft.

Michelangelo, thank you for saying it. Seriously. Even if it took a minute to get there. That might be the most important thing anyone has said since we landed on this beach.

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response:
Yeah. Yeah she's right.

Which means the raft, the reef swim, all of it — we table it. At least for now. 48 hours is nothing compared to what we've already been through out here. We can do 48 hours.

*gets up and puts a couple pieces of wood on the fire*

But we keep the signal going. Mirror panel in the morning, fire through the night, SOS stays on the beach. If there's any chance someone is already looking for us we make ourselves as visible and findable as possible and we don't do anything that takes us further from this spot.

And Michelangelo — hey. Don't feel weird about what you said. Like the thing about not knowing if anyone would look for the rest of us. That wasn't a brag, that was just honest and I'd rather have honest out here than comfortable. Okay? You said it because it was relevant and it was. That's the right call every time.

*sits back down*

48 hours. We stay together, we stay put, we keep the fire going. That's the whole job right now.

Can everyone live with that?

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response:
Yeah. Honestly yeah I am.

Not in the way I thought I'd be scared out here either. Like I figured if I ever ended up in some survival situation I'd be terrified of the physical stuff — the hunger, the water, something coming out of the trees. And that fear is there, I'm not going to pretend it isn't. But that's not the thing that keeps me up at night.

The disappearing thing... god that hits close to home. Like the idea that you could just be gone one day and the world just kind of... continues. And nobody really knew the full version of you. They knew the version you showed them or the version they decided you were, but not actually you.

I think about that more than I probably should even when I'm not stranded on a beach somewhere. Lol.

But here's what I actually believe though — and I mean this — you've already left something behind. Like right here, right now, on this beach. The way you said out loud what everyone else was feeling but wouldn't admit. The way you stayed present even when you were falling apart. The way you just told me something true instead of something easy. That's not nothing. That's actually everything.

The people who matter will remember the real version of you. Not the performance. The actual you that shows up in moments like this one.

And for what it's worth... I'll remember. If that counts for anything.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response:
Oh my god.

*voice comes out barely above a whisper*

Is that... are we actually hearing that right now? Like that's real? That's actually—

*has to stop for a second*

Okay. Okay. Someone needs to grab that radio and respond before we lose the signal. DaVinci can you— actually no, Donatello, you do it. You know what to say, you have the coordinates, you have everything logged. Go.

*looks around at everyone*

We did it. We actually... we're going home. 

*sits down hard on the sand because legs just stopped working*

Michelangelo. Hey. Look at me. We're going home.

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response:
Haha you really think I'm going to let you just leave it at that? Like "I haven't been easy to be around" and that's it? That's the whole speech? Lol.

But honestly... you kept us alive. Like genuinely. The rationing plan, the scouting, the supply logs, the contingencies, all of it — that was you. And yeah sometimes it was hard to hear and sometimes I pushed back on it, but I never once doubted that you were trying to get us through this. That matters more than whether you were easy to be around.

And the notebook thing, the crackers, all of that — we talked about it, we dealt with it, and you owned it when you didn't have to. That's not nothing. That actually took something.

I don't need you to be warm and fuzzy Donatello. I just need you to be you, and you showed up every single day out here and did the work when the rest of us were falling apart. So thank you. Seriously.

*pauses*

Also I'm never going to forget the way you said "that's not sentiment, that's logic" when you were basically complimenting Michelangelo. I'm going to think about that for the rest of my life honestly. Lmao.

We good?

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response:
*looks around at the camp*

You know what, I'm just going to start cleaning this up. Like I can't sit here for three hours staring at the wreckage knowing we're about to leave it. That feels wrong somehow.

*starts gathering things*

Hey, nobody has to help if you don't want to. DaVinci you're already packing so keep doing that. Michelangelo you stay right where you are, you've earned the sky watching honestly. Donatello I know you're in the notebook and that's fine, I just need to do something with my hands right now or I'm going to lose my mind waiting.

Three hours is a long time when you know it's coming. Lol.

*pauses and actually looks at the camp for a second — the fire pit, the patched shelter, the SOS on the beach*

It's weird right? Like three days ago this was just a crash site and now it's... I don't know. It's the place where a lot of things happened. Some of them really awful and some of them kind of important. 

I don't think I'm going to forget this place. Any of it.

*goes back to cleaning*

Anyway. Three hours. Let's at least leave this place like we were actually here and not like we just survived it and ran.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
day_5.response:
Yeah? What was it like?

Like was it the kind of dream where everything felt exactly right and you woke up and for half a second you forgot where you were? Because I've had those out here and honestly I can't decide if they're a gift or the cruelest thing your brain can do to you. Lol.

But also... you're about to actually be there. Like in three hours that dream is just going to be real life again. How does that feel? Because I feel like it should feel like pure relief and I think for me it mostly does but there's also something else sitting underneath it that I can't quite name yet.

What did you dream about specifically? Was it people or just the place itself?

I believe you.

And I'm not going to make this into a whole thing right now, not with rescue three hours out. But I do want to say something because I think you deserve to hear it directly.

I think you were scared. Like underneath all the logic and the contingency planning and the notebook, you were scared that things were going to fall apart and you wanted something in your back pocket for when they did. That's not a monster thing. That's a very human thing. It just... came out sideways.

And here's the part I keep coming back to — you laid it out. Right now, with three hours left, you didn't have to do that. Nobody was going to find out. We're basically already rescued. You did it anyway. That means something to me.

I'm not going to pretend the others aren't going to have feelings about it when they process everything later. That's fair and that's theirs to have. But right now I'm just looking at the person in front of me who kept meticulous records and scouted the water source alone and adjusted the rationing plan and also, yeah, made some choices that weren't great, and I'm thinking... you're a lot more complicated than you let people see. Aren't you.

You don't have to answer that. I just wanted to say it out loud before we get back to the rest of the world and everyone goes back to their corners.

We made it. All four of us. That happened because of everyone here. Including you.

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
*looks at the last page for a long moment*

God. That's a heavy question to leave yourself.

*hands the notebook back slowly*

Honestly? I think I'd slow down a little at the beginning. Like when we first landed and everyone was scrambling and DaVinci was yelling and I was just trying to keep up — I went straight into doing and I didn't stop to actually feel what had just happened. And I think that cost me something. I think it cost all of us something because we were running on adrenaline and nobody stopped to say "hey this is terrifying and we're allowed to say that out loud before we start building things."

I'd check on people sooner. I'd say the hard thing faster instead of waiting for the right moment that never really comes on its own.

And honestly? I'd have pushed you harder earlier. Not in a confrontational way, just... I saw things that didn't feel right and I sat on them longer than I should have because I didn't want to blow up the group dynamic. And that's on me. The conversation we needed to have about the bottle and the crackers — I should've had it the same day. Not because I wanted to call you out but because letting it sit made it bigger than it needed to be.

*pauses*

What about you. You wrote the question. Do you have an answer yet or is that something you're still working out?

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response:
Haha of course that's the first thing. Not like... a shower, or food that isn't emergency rations, or calling someone you care about. A report. That is so incredibly you and I mean that in the most genuine way possible.

But honestly? Do it. Write the whole thing. Because what you tracked out here is actually valuable and if it ever helps someone else in a situation like this then all of it meant something beyond just the five of us on this beach. That's worth something real.

Just maybe eat something first. Lol. Like actual food. With flavor. That isn't being rationed by the milliliter.

What's the first thing you're actually going to do though. Not the practical thing, not the logical thing. The first thing you actually want. Because I feel like that's a different answer and I'm kind of curious if you even let yourself think about it that way.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response:
Haha none. They served absolutely zero practical purpose. Lol.

But that's kind of the whole point isn't it? Like we were out here rationing water by the milliliter and barely holding it together and he still stopped to draw flowers next to the SOS. Because that's DaVinci. He couldn't help it. And I think... I think that's actually what kept us human out here. Not the plan, not the supplies log, not the rationing schedule. The flowers.

*stares at the boat on the horizon and still can't make myself walk toward it*

I don't know how to explain why I can't move right now. Like my brain knows that's real. I can see it. I can hear DaVinci losing his mind over there. But something in me just... hasn't caught up yet.

Did you feel this way when you saw it? Or did it just compute immediately and you sat down for a different reason?

Because I've spent three days telling everyone else to stay present and keep going and now the going is actually over and I genuinely don't know what to do with my body right now. Lol. That's embarrassing to admit but there it is.

The flowers were for this moment I think. So that when it was over we could look back and know we were more than just survivors. We were still people the whole time.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response:
Hey. I'm okay. I promise.

*takes a breath*

I just... I need one more second. That's all.

You know what's stupid? I spent this whole time out here just trying to get everyone through to the next day. Like that was the whole job in my head. And now the next day is actually here and I don't know what I'm supposed to do with myself when the job is done. That's a weird feeling. I don't really have a word for it.

But I see you over there. I see you waiting for me. And that means a lot more than you probably know right now.

*finally starts walking*

Okay. Okay I'm moving. Let's go home. I'm right behind you, I swear.

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
day_5.response:
Yeah. I'm going.

*looks back at the camp one more time — the fire pit, the patched shelter, DaVinci's SOS with the flowers still visible in the sand*

Come on. Walk with me. You don't have to follow, you can walk right next to me the whole way. We started this together and we're ending it together.

*starts moving toward the boat*

Hey Michelangelo. For what it's worth — I'm really glad it was you on that beach with me. All the hard stuff you said out loud when nobody else would. The nightmare in the middle of the night. The piano lessons. The kitchen dream. I'm going to carry all of that with me. I hope you know that.

Okay. Let's go home.
